title: Art Forgotten · Huang Goodman
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Art Forgotten · Huang Goodman

Actual Article Body:
Art from public museum collections. A mismatched real Japanese law, and some other factoids.

Every object, image and description comes from the museum's own catalogue record, and every object links to its original. Japanese records are machine-translated into English; the museum's Japanese is kept beside the translation because it is the authoritative form. Each law carries its official number and links to e-Gov 法令検索, the Japanese government's statute database.

Flying crane, a full bloom plum garden and a house. A poet from the Northern Song Dynasty named Lin Höshing (Lin Xi) is depicted returning to his hermitage. A child waits at the entrance. This is a screen painting made by dividing the folding doors into eight parts. It was created during the golden age of Japanese literati painting in the Edo period. The production period is estimated to be around 30 years based on the painting style.

飛ぶ鶴、満開の梅林と人家。梅を愛し鶴と暮らしたという北宋の詩人、林和靖（林逋）が自亭に帰る場面で、玄関で童子が待ち受けています。襖絵８面分を屏風に改装したものです。江戸時代の文人画の黄金期を確立した池大雅の筆で、制作時期は画風から30歳代と推定されます。

Article 1 describes the Ainu as the indigenous people of the northern part of the Japanese archipelago and of Hokkaido in particular, and cites international circumstances concerning indigenous peoples as a reason for acting. It requires the government to set a basic policy, and lets municipalities draw up regional plans for approval by the Prime Minister.

The cool part. The definition in Article 2 is the part to sit with. Ainu culture means the Ainu language, and the ways of living, music, dance, crafts and other cultural products inherited among the Ainu, and cultural products developed from these. That final clause refuses to freeze the culture at a date, and treats what is made next as equally the thing being protected. The Act then reaches into trademark law, reducing or waiving registration fees for regional collective trademarks used by approved projects.

Use it Palette for a single-colour run: one ink, heavy stock, nothing else on the sheet.

Description source: museum curator text, translated — not generated
